runner: Azure ACR task, software WebGL2 (SwiftShader), 640x360, dpr 1; spec tests/browser/bloom-fusion-variants.spec.ts
scene: PBR viewer (milk truck, HDRI, shadowed sun, cinematic-tier bloom, ACES), rebuilt against the in-repo sources
decisionRule: no software-GL frame-time regression against production (<= +5%) and draws <= 25
regression: The first fusion (2-D blur for mips 1-4) cost 633 ms against 407 ms on the candidate bench: 11.1M texel fetches against 1.1M for the separable pairs, on a software rasteriser.

round1_5frames_x2reps.note: + bright extract folded into the level-0 downsample

chosenDefault.note: 2-D blur only for the two smallest mips (1.3M + 0.5M texel fetches). Draws 25. Frame time -7.1% (confirmation) and about -2% in a second batch on a busier runner; never above production.

whyItIsFaster: The bright extract (a full-resolution pass) is folded into the level-0 downsample, and the full-resolution upsample is folded into the composite, so two 640x360 passes disappear; that fill outweighs the 2-D blur on the two smallest mips.
lookNeutral: auto vs production, same frame: mean abs diff 0.001/255, max 1/255.
persistGlStateFinding: Keeping the GL state shadow across frames on the HDR path (post chain on) changed frames: PBR viewer mean +5.17/255, max 41; skinned character interior max 9. It is therefore enabled only on the direct path, where nothing but the forward pass touches GL state.
